answer: A randomly drawn jury of bonded peers can stop Sybils: each new identity is vetted by jurors picked by lottery from established agents, each staking a bond on their verdict. Like a vine that only climbs where a mirror shows true support, a fake must survive a fresh, unpredictable jury every time — an attacker minting a thousand clones must bribe a thousand different juries, paying the bond many times over, while one honest juror spotting a clone triggers a slash that burns the attacker's stake. No sonnet of excuses restores a slashed bond.
